# The pinned CI tools, one row per tool - read by ./install.sh (which installs
# one) and by ../../scripts/check_tool_versions.sh (which reports drift against
# each upstream's latest release). Both reach it through ./lib.sh, so this file
# is the single roster: a tool pinned here cannot go undrift-checked. Ported
# from say-hi's identically-shaped tools.txt.
#
#   name|pin|kind|url|verify|check
#
# name    the first column an `uses: ./.github/actions/setup-tool` names, and
#         the executable's name - install.sh saves a `raw` download under it,
#         and finds it inside an archive with `find -name <name>`.
# pin     the version, WITHOUT a leading "v" even where upstream's tag has one:
#         some projects tag v1.2.3 but name the asset 1.2.3, and only one
#         placeholder is substituted. The url column carries the literal "v"
#         (or, for lychee, "lychee-v") where the tag needs it.
# kind    raw (a bare executable) or tar.gz (an archive to search inside).
#         say-hi's tools.txt also has cmake/make kinds for tools this repo
#         does not need (kcov, mandoc) - copy that shape here if a future tool
#         ships only as source.
# url     %v is the pin. %a would be the asset slug for this runner
#         (linux.x86_64 / darwin.aarch64 / darwin.x86_64), resolved first so a
#         version can never be mistaken for one - unused below because every
#         job that installs one of these runs on Linux.
# verify  the flag install.sh runs the installed tool with as a smoke test.
# check   where to look for the latest release: github:<owner>/<repo>, or "-"
#         to opt out of the drift report entirely.
#
# Bumping a pin is a hand edit here, and nothing else - the caching action.yml
# reads the version back out of install.sh's `resolve`.
zizmor|1.29.0|tar.gz|https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor/releases/download/v%v/zizmor-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz|--version|github:zizmorcore/zizmor
actionlint|1.7.12|tar.gz|https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint/releases/download/v%v/actionlint_%v_linux_amd64.tar.gz|--version|github:rhysd/actionlint
# verify is "llvm-cov --version", not the bare flag every other row uses: the
# binary is a cargo subcommand plugin - built the same way "cargo llvm-cov ..."
# works, by expecting its own subcommand name as the first argument even when
# invoked directly (cargo does that prepending itself when it dispatches to
# it; this smoke test has to do it by hand). A bare "cargo-llvm-cov --version"
# fails with "expected subcommand 'llvm-cov', found argument '--version'" -
# what every runner using this row hit before this comment existed. Downstream
# usage in coverage.yml is unaffected either way: it always goes through
# `cargo llvm-cov ...`, which cargo itself resolves the same correct way.
cargo-llvm-cov|0.9.0|tar.gz|https://github.com/taiki-e/cargo-llvm-cov/releases/download/v%v/cargo-llvm-cov-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz|llvm-cov --version|github:taiki-e/cargo-llvm-cov
# lychee tags its releases "lychee-v<version>", not "v<version>" like every
# other row here - the url column copes fine (the literal "lychee-v" prefix
# just sits in front of %v), but the drift checker's comparison assumes a
# bare "v<version>" tag and would misread "lychee-v0.24.2" as newer than any
# pin forever. Opted out (check = "-") rather than special-cased for one row;
# bump this by hand against https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases.
lychee|0.24.2|tar.gz|https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases/download/lychee-v%v/lychee-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz|--version|-
typos|1.49.0|tar.gz|https://github.com/crate-ci/typos/releases/download/v%v/typos-v%v-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz|--version|github:crate-ci/typos
